_comment: The billing provider is 'meta'; the coding-agent adapter is 'muse'; the
pseudo-adapter holding the consent row is 'muse-account-api'. Three
which spells ProviderMeta 'distinct from the muse adapter name'.
This is the account-API half of what issue #2008 extracts from. Its
quota_windows axis is source-specific-unavailable, NOT unassessed: the
one authorized live probe returned 200 with an active subscription, a
named tier, and no usage field of any kind. A schema that could not
express that would express Muse as an incomplete provider.

redaction.note: The raw response carries fourteen top-level keys including api_key, user_email and user_full_name. Only these two are ever retained; the live-probe fixture records the other names, never their values.

fixtures.name: account-api-response
fixtures.note: The redacted body from the 2026-09-20 live probe, verbatim.

billing_mode.note: is_subs_active plus subs_tier_name identify the billed product.

quota_windows.note: 200 OK on an active subscription with no subs_usage key at all. This says nothing about whether Muse has a quota source elsewhere — only that this route does not carry one (#1977 §5).

balance.note: No balance or credit route has been probed for this provider.

account_identity.note: The response carries no stable provider account id, so accountRef() returns the empty string by construction and the poller falls back to a session-scoped key — which is a degradation in Irrlicht's dedup, not a property of the product. The product's quota_scope above stays "account" for that reason: it says what the subscription bills against, not what Irrlicht can currently key on. Hashing the access token was rejected as an account id.

evidence.note: Issue #2007's one authorized live request, Muse Code 1.3.0 (1.3.0-R3401.1), redacted before it was written.
